subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Central nervous system tumours: key diagnostic and treatment points

steps.tx: Diffuse gliomas are classified using **IDH status** first. IDH mutant tumours carry a better outlook than IDH wildtype tumours. The IDH mutation produces the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate, which can be detected on magnetic resonance spectroscopy. Under WHO CNS5, IDH wildtype diffuse astrocytic tumours with glioblastoma features are graded as glioblastoma even when histology looks lower grade.

steps.tx: Oligodendroglioma is defined by an **IDH mutation** together with **1p/19q codeletion**. These tumours are often frontal and seizure-presenting, and they respond well to chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Vorasidenib, an IDH inhibitor, has shown benefit in the INDIGO trial for grade 2 IDH mutant gliomas, delaying progression. Subtotal debulking still helps seizure control and survival when complete resection is not possible.

steps.tx: PCV is a three-drug chemotherapy combination used as an adjuvant option for anaplastic oligodendroglioma and 1p19q codeleted gliomas. Treatment usually runs for around six cycles, since **myelosuppression** accumulates over time, mainly causing low white cells and platelets. Clinicians should also recall that **radiation necrosis** is a late effect of cranial irradiation, so new enhancement after treatment may reflect injury rather than progression.

steps.tx: **Medulloblastoma** is the most common malignant **posterior fossa tumour** in children and arises in the **cerebellum**. It often causes **raised intracranial pressure** and can seed through **cerebrospinal fluid**, so whole spine **MRI** is required at staging. Under **WHO CNS5**, it is classified by **molecular subgroup** (WNT, SHH, group 3 and group 4) rather than histology alone.

steps.tx: Primary CNS lymphoma, mostly diffuse large B-cell type, is seen in immunocompetent and immunosuppressed patients. Steroids can kill lymphoma cells, so biopsy should be done before dexamethasone where possible. Brain metastases preferentially lodge at the **gray-white junction**, while meningiomas are dural-based with a dural tail and do not invade brain tissue.
